narrative:
On August 25, 2026, the Karnataka High Court achieved an overall hearing rate of 44.2%, taking up 1,135 of the 2,569 matters scheduled across 47 benches. This reflects a steady improvement over recent sittings, surpassing the hearing rates recorded on August 20 (38.5%), August 19 (42.0%), and August 18 (43.3%).

Workload distribution and clearance varied significantly among individual benches. Justice S. Vishwajith Shetty in Hall 19 handled the highest absolute volume, hearing 118 out of 240 scheduled cases (49.2%), closely followed by Justice M. Nagaprasanna in Hall 14, who heard 115 out of 197 matters (58.4%). Strong disposal rates on medium-sized dockets were posted by Justice E.S. Indiresh (75.0%) and Justice Chillakur Sumalatha (73.1%). In contrast, several lists saw no movement, including Hall 1 under the Chief Justice and Justice K.S. Hemalekha (0 heard of 59 scheduled across two cause lists) and Hall 15 under Justice Ravi (0 heard of 51 scheduled).

By procedural stage, Orders formed the core of the daily docket, with 437 of 978 cases heard (44.7%), while Admission stages achieved a 49.7% conversion rate (267 of 537). Final Hearing matters progressed at a slower pace of 31.1% (128 of 412 heard), though this improved upon the 22.8% to 29.4% range observed in preceding sessions.

Writ Petitions (WP) dominated the case profile, with 438 of 1,056 listings taken up (41.5%), followed by Miscellaneous First Appeals (MFA) at 38.8% (205 of 529). Criminal Petitions (CRL.P) and Regular Second Appeals (RSA) recorded healthy clearance rates of 54.1% and 62.9%, respectively. Conversely, Commercial Appeals (COMAP) faced severe bottlenecks, registering a conversion rate of just 10.2% (6 of 59 heard).
